A docs site is a folder of Markdown and one YAML file. This page lists every block a page can use: the Markdown you write, then the block as this site draws it. Pages that aiui build publishes also exist as plain Markdown (/docs/ .md, components converted) and in llms.txt, so assistants read the same content (AI-ready docs).

site.theme.preset picks the colours. paper is the look of this site: warm paper, a navy accent, serif titles, 17px text on a 1.7 line height and a measure of about 75 characters. mode: system follows the reader's OS. The other presets and what each changes are in Theming.

YAML at the top of a page sets its title in the sidebar, the browser tab and search results, and its description for search engines and llms.txt. Every key is optional, and the common MDX page metadata keys work as they are. Key Type What it does title string The page title: the # heading when the body has none, the browser tab, search, llms.txt. Default: the first # heading, else the file name. description string Shown under the title (unless the first paragraph already says it), and the meta description, llms.txt and search snippet. Default: the first paragraph, for those but not shown again. sidebarTitle (or nav_title) string A shorter label in the sidebar. icon string Before the sidebar label: a lucide name (rocket, terminal, book-open, …), an emoji, or an image URL (https://… or /icons/x.svg). tag string A badge after the sidebar label, such as NEW or BETA. deprecated true/false true: a Deprecated badge, the label struck through, and a notice above the page. mode string wide: no "On this page", a wider column. center: no sidebar either. custom: only the article, full width (no breadcrumb, footer or pager). frame: custom with the sidebar. assistant: the page's text, then Ask AI under it. url string An https:// URL makes the page a sidebar link that opens that site in a new tab. The page itself is not published (no route, sitemap, llms.txt or search entry). hideFooterPagination true/false true: no previous / next links under the page. noAnchor true/false true: no copy-link icon on the page's headings. order number Position inside its folder (default: a number prefix such as 01-). hidden true/false Routable, but not in the sidebar, pager or indexes (Navigation). noindex true/false Tells search engines not to index the page (and leaves it out of the sitemap). searchable true/false false leaves the page out of the site's own search. keywords list of words, or one comma-separated string Extra search terms, matched but never shown; also the keywords meta tag and JSON-LD. canonical string The page's canonical URL (and og:url), for a page whose original lives elsewhere. robots string The robots meta, such as noindex, nofollow; a value with noindex also leaves the page out of the sitemap, llms.txt and search. og:*, twitter:*, article:* string That head tag for this page (quote the key: 'og:image': /images/card.png); see SEO. boost number Search ranking weight (2 ranks the page higher). openapi string "GET /users", "spec.yaml POST /users" or "webhook name": the page shows that operation, its endpoint bar, Try it, fields and examples around your text (OpenAPI). api string "POST /v1/users": an endpoint page without a spec, Try it from the page's s (OpenAPI). playground string interactive, simple, none or auth: the Try-it display of an openapi: or api: page; site-wide: api.playground.display (OpenAPI). timestamp true/false Turns the "Last updated" date off or on for this page (see Page footer). lastUpdatedDate date (2026-05-01) The "Last updated" date, instead of the last commit's. related list of pages or URLs, or false The "Related pages" under this page, instead of the suggested ones; false shows none (Related pages). pageActions list of page actions, or false This page's page actions menu, in order, instead of the site's; false shows none (Page actions). rss true/false true on a changelog page: the build writes its entries as an RSS feed at /rss.xml and links it (Changelog). public true/false On a site with sign-in: true opens the page to everyone, false keeps it behind sign-in when a public pattern would open it. groups list of group names, or one name On a site with sign-in: only readers in one of these groups can read the page; to everyone else it does not exist. layout, hero, features The docs home page (Home page layout). any other key string, number or true/false Custom data, such as product: cloud: a data-fm-product="cloud" attribute on the article (for CSS) and meta in the aiui:content-loaded event (for custom JS). The front matter never shows on the page as text. aiui validate checks these types and reports the line of a wrong one (hidden: "yes" is a string, so the page would stay in the sidebar), front matter that is not valid YAML, images without alt text, two files that publish the same page, two sidebar entries with the same title in one folder, headings that skip a level, empty pages and a theme.accent with too little contrast. Each finding names file:line and how to fix it; --strict makes them errors for CI. See the codes. A nav group can also list a link among its pages:

## and ### headings build the "On this page" list beside the article (above it on narrow screens), which follows the reader as they scroll. Every heading gets an id from its text, so writing-docs#callouts links straight to a section, and a link with a section opens the page scrolled to it. Hover a heading (on a phone, look beside it) for its link icon: one click puts the section in the address bar and copies its URL. Keep one # title per page; the paragraph right under it is the lede and reads larger. To pin an anchor that survives a reworded title, end the heading with {#id}: ## Install the CLI {#install} links as #install, the search index uses the same id, and the braces never show.

Pages written for MkDocs keep working: !!! note "Title" with an indented body draws the same callout (note, info, tip, success, warning, danger and the other MkDocs types).

For a procedure the reader follows in order. Each step gets a number on a rail; its body is ordinary Markdown, code blocks included. Reply to every message with @aiui.reply. aiui run app.py, then open the address it prints. with one per choice: the same task in different tools, languages or operating systems. Arrow keys move between tabs. Run export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-... before aiui run. Fence code with its language for highlighting and a copy button. 74 languages are highlighted, each grammar loaded only when a page uses it; the rest show as plain text unless the site adds its own grammar (code theme and languages). Comments are drawn in a colour that keeps 4.5:1 contrast on the code background, light and dark. Highlighted: apache, astro, awk, bash, bat, bicep, c, clojure, cmake, cpp, csharp, css, csv, dart, diff, docker, dotenv, elixir, elm, fish, fsharp, gleam, glsl, go, graphql, groovy, handlebars, haskell, hcl, html, http, ini, java, javascript, jinja, json, jsonl, jsx, julia, kotlin, lua, make, markdown, matlab, nginx, nix, objective-c, perl, php, powershell, prisma, proto, python, r, regexp, ruby, rust, sass, scala, scss, solidity, sql, svelte, swift, terraform, toml, tsx, typescript, vb, vue, wgsl, xml, yaml and zig, with their common short names (sh, js, ts, py, yml, tf, ps1, makefile, objc, protobuf, hs, ex and more).

After the language, name the file with title="…" (or just the name) and pick lines to highlight with {…}: single lines and ranges, separated by commas. Without title=, every word after the language up to the first option is the title: python Reply handler {3-4} shows "Reply handler". highlight={3-4}, hl_lines="3 4" and highlight="3-4" work too, so fences written for MkDocs or in MDX syntax carry over.

Options go after the language, in any order, alone or together: Option What it does lines Line numbers in a gutter (the copy button copies the code only). wrap Long lines wrap instead of scrolling sideways. expandable A block over 12 lines shows 12 and a "Show all N lines" button. nocopy No copy button. icon="terminal" An icon before the title (terminal, code, rocket, …; other names show the code icon). highlight={1-2,5} Highlighted lines; {1-2,5} alone does the same. focus={2,4-5} These lines stay sharp, the rest dim until the reader points at the block. A flag is never taken for a title, and twoslash is accepted and ignored.

End a line with a [!code …] comment in the language's own comment syntax (//, #, --, `) to mark it:++added,-- removed, highlight and focus. :N marks that line and the next N-1; a comment on a line of its own marks the lines after it. The comments never show, and the copy button copies the code without them.

Write a block once and use it on many pages. Put it in docs/snippets/ (that folder is never published as pages) and include it where it should appear: docs/snippets/install.md, where {pkg} takes the value passed in: Site-wide values go in one key of aiui.yaml, and {{name}} in any page or snippet becomes the value, in text, code and front matter (title, description): Snippets nest, and take any number of props. A path is looked up next to the page, then in docs/snippets/, then the docs folder; /x.md starts at the docs folder. Indent the tag inside a list item and the snippet follows the indent. Existing MDX snippet syntax works too: import Install from '/snippets/install.mdx' then . From MkDocs: --8<-- "install.md" on a line of its own. Write \{{name}} for a literal {{name}}. A snippet tag in a code block stays as written. It all happens in aiui build, so the page, its .md copy, llms-full.txt and search all hold the expanded text. A missing snippet, a path outside the project folder, or a snippet that includes itself fails the build (7008), and aiui validate names each {{name}} that has no value (7007). To publish a docs folder that is really called snippets, add "!snippets" to content.docs.exclude.

A changelog page is a list of entries, newest first. Add rss: true and readers can subscribe: label (a date or version) is the entry's section heading: it gets an anchor (#2026-11-18, or id="…"), a copy-link icon, a line in "On this page" and its own result in site search. From 768px wide it sits in a left column that stays in view while the entry scrolls. description shows under the label, tags ({["A", "B"]} or "A, B") as chips. A page with tagged entries gets a tag filter above the first entry. Choosing tags shows the entries with any of them and keeps the choice in the address (?tags=API,Fix), so a filtered view is a link you can share. rss: true: aiui build writes /rss.xml (RSS 2.0, one item per entry: the label and description as its title, the entry's anchor as its link, its tags as categories and its body as HTML; a label that is a date, such as 2026-11-18 or November 18, 2026, becomes its date). The page's head gets , so browsers and feed readers find it, and the filter row shows an "RSS feed" link. Links are absolute when the site URL is known (seo.siteUrl or a CNAME file), base path included. The entries are ## label sections in the page's .md and llms-full.txt.

Tags work the way MDX reads them: on lines of their own, on one line with their text, inside a list item (indent the tag with the item's text), or self-closing (). Attributes take quotes or braces (cols={3}) and may run over several lines. A body indented under its tag is text, not code, as in MDX. A tag the site does not know (say ) keeps its text as plain Markdown, and aiui build and aiui validate name it: Warning: docs/guide.md:12: is not a docs component; its content shows as plain Markdown. / for="agents" shows its content only on the page / only to agents (AI-ready docs).

Write a React component once and use it on any page as a tag. Point the site at one ES module beside aiui.yaml: The module registers each component with registerBlock from @aiui/sdk, or exports it under the tag's name. It imports React and the SDK as bare names: the build maps them to the page's own copies, so no bundler is needed for plain JS, and hooks work. Props. A quoted attribute is a string; {…} is a value: a number, true or false, an array or an object ({{ calls: 10 }}, JSON or JS-style); a bare attribute () is true. The component gets them as props, and as node.props like any block. Children. The tag's body is Markdown, rendered and passed as children. A self-closing tag that shares its line with text sits inside the sentence. Loading. The module loads only on a page that uses one of its tags, after the page has painted; until then, and if the module fails or the component throws, the page shows the tag's body. A built-in tag name (, ) keeps its built-in meaning. Tags. The build finds them in the module (registerBlock('Name' and export function Name). A minified bundle hides them: list them with site.components: {src: ./components/index.js, tags: [Counter, Price]}. Declared tags are not reported as unknown; a missing module, or one with no tag the build can find, is a 7021 warning. Security. The module is your site's own code, served from the site (script-src 'self'); the build adds the import map's hash to the Content-Security-Policy. Only same-site modules load. In the .md copy for agents the tag's body stays and the tag goes. Styles. Use the theme's CSS variables (var(--primary)), or add a stylesheet with site.customCss. An installed UI plugin whose blocks() include a type named like a component (HelloCard) provides that tag too, with no config: when a page uses a tag nothing else knows, the build asks the plugins and publishes the plugin's static folder with the site.

Add className (or class) to a component tag or to raw HTML to adjust one block: its spacing, width, text, colour or layout. The classes use the site's theme tokens, so they follow light and dark mode and any theme preset: Only these classes work ({a,b} means either). Any other class is dropped, and aiui validate and aiui build name it with its file and line, with the nearest allowed class (finding 7022). Readers press ⌘ K ( Ctrl K ) or the search field. Search covers page titles, every ## and ### heading and all the text under it, and a result opens the page at its section with the words marked. It forgives typing: plurals and verb forms match ("themes", "theming"), a word matches as you type it ("inst"), one typo in a longer word still matches, and question words drop out ("how do I deploy"). Titles rank first, then headings, then text, each BM25 style. While the dialog is open the address bar carries the query, so a link such as /docs?q=api+keys opens search filled in. On a site with header tabs (Navigation), chips filter results by tab: search starts in the reader's tab, and one row offers the other tabs' results when it has none. A navigation group's boost: applies to its pages (a page's own wins). Site settings (search.provider is ignored and aiui validate says so): aiui build writes the index (search-index.json, up to 6,000 characters per section) and the same index in parts under search-index/, so the dialog downloads only what a query needs: Part Holds Fetched search-index/meta.json each page's path, keywords, boost and section headings with their word counts, and the sorted list of every word the first time a reader opens search search-index/ /w .json for a run of those words, the sections each appears in and how often when a query has a word in that run (by stem, prefix or one typo) search-index/ /p .json page i's section text when the page is in the results, for its snippets Ranking is the same as over the whole file: BM25, stems, prefixes, typos, keywords, boost and the tab chips. On this repository's 99 searchable pages the first open downloads 35 KB gzipped instead of 181 KB, and a first query about 13 KB more. is a hash of the index, so a page cached from an older deploy never mixes parts; a missing part, or a site built before the parts existed, makes the dialog read search-index.json whole, which every other reader (the MCP server, Ask AI, older pages) still uses. A site with sign-in gets no parts: its search-index.json is cut per reader.

Link to another page by its file: Theming. The build turns it into the page's URL, so links work on GitHub and on the site. A folder's README.md or index.md is served at the folder's URL (protocols/adp/README.md at /docs/protocols/adp), and a number prefix is dropped (adr/0003-selectable-layouts.md at /docs/adr/selectable-layouts). List such a page in the nav by its file path (protocols/adp/README); the header still opens the tab that lists it.

aiui docs check-links finds every link that leads nowhere, before readers do: It checks Markdown links and images, reference links, href and src on components and HTML (, , ), the docs home hero and features links, the nav page entries and the navbar and footer links in the YAML. A #section link is checked against the ids the site gives its headings (## The aiui CLI is #the-aiui-cli). Links in code are skipped. Paths outside the docs (app routes such as /chat) are not judged. --external also requests every http(s) URL, and --json prints the result for scripts. The exit code is 1 when a link is broken, so a CI step needs one line. aiui validate --strict and aiui build --strict fail on broken links too; without --strict they print them as warnings.

Above every page's title, Copy page copies the page's Markdown, ready to paste into an assistant. Ctrl+C (⌘C on a Mac) does the same when nothing is selected and the cursor is not in a text field. Its menu also has: Action Id What it does Copy page copy The page's agent-ready Markdown on the clipboard View as Markdown view Opens /docs/ .md, the page as plain Markdown for assistants Download as PDF pdf The browser's Print dialog; pick Save as PDF Listen to page listen The browser reads the article aloud, with pause and stop; hidden where the browser has no speech Open in ChatGPT chatgpt A new ChatGPT chat that reads the page and takes questions Open in Claude claude The same, in Claude Copy MCP server URL, Connect to Cursor / VS Code mcp On a site aiui serve runs (MCP server) Nothing to configure: they use the Markdown aiui build already publishes. Try it on this page. To pick and order the actions, list them. Besides the ids above there are perplexity, grok, google (Google AI Mode), copilot, mistral (Le Chat) and cursor, and links of your own: In href, {url} is the page's address, {md} its Markdown, {title} its title and {prompt} the "read this page" prompt the assistants get, each URL-encoded. pageActions: false turns the menu off. One page can have its own list, or none, in its front matter:

A printed page (Download as PDF, or the browser's own Print, Ctrl+P / ⌘P) is the article alone, on light paper even when the reader uses dark mode: The header, sidebar, "On this page", page actions, previous / next, footer and feedback are left out. Breadcrumbs and "Last updated" stay. Everything a click would reveal is shown: accordions, field lists and file trees open, every tab of and prints under its own title, and expandable code blocks print every line. Code wraps instead of running off the page; code blocks, callouts, cards, steps, table rows and images are not split across pages. External links print their address after the link text: link (https://example.com/docs). Site chrome added by custom JS (site.customJs) or a plugin can opt out of print with data-print="hide". The PDF comes from the reader's browser: no build step, no server-side renderer.

Under each page: "Was this page helpful?" (on by default, see Page feedback) and two optional parts, turned on in aiui.yaml: Edit this page links to pattern with :path replaced by the page's file under the docs folder (getting-started/quickstart.md). Last updated is the date of the last commit that changed the page. aiui build reads it from git. In a shallow clone, pages changed inside the cloned history keep their date; older ones get none rather than the clone's date. In GitHub Actions, check out with fetch-depth: 0 to date every page. A page's lastUpdatedDate: 2026-05-01 sets the date by hand, and timestamp: false (or true) turns it off (or on) for that page alone. Was this page helpful? keeps the vote (next section). With issues, a "No" also offers a new issue there with the page's title and address filled in. The footer of this page shows all three.

Under each page, "Related pages" lists the three pages closest to it. Nothing to configure: aiui build compares the words of every page (title, keywords, description and headings count most, then the text) and favours pages in the same sidebar group. Hidden, noindex and searchable: false pages and the home page are never suggested. The list is part of docs-nav.json, so it works on any static host and offline, and each page's agent-ready .md ends with it too. Pick the list for a page in its front matter, or turn it off: related: false shows none on that page. Site-wide, content.docs.related: 5 shows five (at most 10) and content.docs.related: false only the lists pages set themselves. aiui validate reports a target that is no page (7013). The block is left out when the page prints.

Nothing to configure: under aiui serve and aiui dev every docs page asks "Was this page helpful?". A vote is stored at once; the reader can then add a comment (up to 1,000 characters), which joins that vote. Read them with: Votes are lines of docs-feedback/feedback.jsonl in the data directory ($AIUI_DATA_DIR, default ~/.praisonaiui). POST /api/docs/feedback takes same-origin requests only (plus --cors-origins, AIUI_ALLOWED_ORIGINS), checks the Host header, takes 4 KiB and 20 posts a minute per client, and stops at 20 MB. Nothing is readable over HTTP; the export is the CLI. Agents report through the docs MCP server's submit_feedback tool into the same store and limits (MCP server). A code flag is a -1 vote with kind: "code" and block, the block's index on the page, plus an optional comment. aiui serve and aiui dev say in the ui-config.json they serve where they keep votes (docsFeedback.url); a static host (GitHub Pages, any CDN) serves the built file, which has no such entry, so with no endpoint the page sends no request at all and the question is shown only if issues is set. endpoint receives the vote as JSON, sent as text/plain when it is on another origin so the browser makes no preflight request: {"id", "path", "value", "kind", "block", "comment"}. A comment arrives as a second post with the same id. Every vote, wherever it goes, also fires a browser event your own script can send to analytics:

File What it holds /llms.txt every page with its description, by nav group (llmstxt.org) /llms-full.txt every page's agent-ready Markdown in one file /docs/ .md one page's agent-ready Markdown (AI-ready docs) /docs/ .source.md the page source the site renders /search-index.json headings and text per page, for the site's own search /search-index/ the same index in parts, fetched as a query needs them (Search) /sitemap.xml, /robots.txt for search engines Each page's HTML also carries that page's source (a JSON script, id="aiui-initial-doc"), so the first visit renders without a second request for it. Pages over 200 KB of Markdown are fetched as before. It also carries docs-nav.json and route-manifest.json (id="aiui-boot-data", each up to 100 KB; not the navigation of a site with sign-in) and preloads ui-config.json; see Deploy to GitHub Pages → How pages load.
